content: Larva migrans refers to a group of conditions caused by the migration of nematode larvae within human tissues. These conditions are classified into several types based on the affected area and the specific nematode species involved: 1. Cutaneous larva migrans: This is a dermatological condition caused by the larvae of various nematode parasites. It is characterized by serpiginous, erythematous tracks on the skin, which result from the subcutaneous migration of the larvae. 2. Visceral larva migrans: This condition primarily affects children and occurs when nematode larvae migrate through internal organs such as the liver, lungs, and other tissues. It is often associated with species like Toxocara canis or Toxocara cati. 3. Ocular larva migrans: This is an ocular manifestation of larva migrans syndrome, occurring when nematode larvae invade the eye. It can lead to visual disturbances, retinal damage, and in severe cases, blindness. 4. Larva migrans profundus (Gnathostomiasis): This is a deeper tissue infection caused by the larvae of nematodes such as Gnathostoma spinigerum. It can involve subcutaneous tissues, muscles, and even the central nervous system. Diagnosis Physical Examination The diagnosis of larva migrans, particularly cutaneous larva migrans, is often based on clinical presentation. The characteristic serpiginous tracks on the skin are a hallmark feature and are typically adapted from dermatological references such as the Dermatology Atlas. Repeated observations and documentation of these tracks are essential for confirming the diagnosis and monitoring the progression of the condition.
